newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraq says distribution plan ready but delayed.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says distribution plan ready but delayed.

text.p: A senior Iraqi official at the United Nations said on Wednesday that the aid distribution plan was ready for submission but that oil sales under the U.N. "oil-for-food" deal would not begin until the money currently held in an escrow account was spent.

The oil deal was renewed two weeks ago but oil sales for the second month period beginning June 8 cannot begin until the distribution plan and a pricing formula for oil contracts is submitted to the U.N.
Iraq has complained repeatedly to the U.N. about delays in the approval of aid contracts, which Baghdad blames on U.S. intransigence.
There is currently about $800 million of oil sales proceeds in an escrow account which cannot be spent until aid contracts are approved.
"The distribution plan and its annexes are ready. We are waiting to finalize all procedures," said the Iraqi official, who asked not to be named.
Asked when Iraq will resume selling oil, the official said: "Not until all of the funds are exhausted, all $800 million."
